domain_label: Plated Jewelry Form — Sizing & Fit Standards, Fit Tolerance & the Sizing-to-Returns Link
purpose: A method for reasoning about the standard sizing systems and fit dimensions of fashion/plated jewelry (ring sizing systems, chain/necklace lengths, hoop diameters and earring post gauges, bracelet/bangle sizing), the fit tolerance and plating-specific dimensional constraints that govern them, and the causal link from sizing to returns/exchanges — so a plated-jewelry launch can rank which categories structurally minimize sizing-driven returns [METHOD] on top of genuine size-standard facts [FACT], without inventing return rates or size distributions.
assumptions: the category & construction taxonomy (studs/hoops/drops; chains/pendants/chokers; rings/bands; bracelets/bangles/cuffs; anklets) is inherited from kb1_category_construction_taxonomy and accepted as input, not re-derived here

size-standard facts are cited public/industry standards: US ring numeric sizing with ~2.55mm circumference (~0.81mm diameter) per full size and ISO 8653 inside-circumference-in-mm sizing [FACT]; standard necklace length bands choker 14-16 in / princess 17-19 in / matinee 20-24 in / opera 28-36 in / rope 36 in+ [FACT-industry]; standard earring post gauge ~20-21 ga (~0.71-0.81mm) and standard lobe piercing 20 ga (~0.8mm) / 18 ga (~1.0mm) [FACT]; EN1811 nickel-release limit 0.5 ug/cm2/week [FACT]

plating is a thin surface layer (microns) whose dimensional effect on fit is negligible but whose mechanical fragility is decisive: resizing a plated ring abrades/breaks the plating and forces re-plating, so plated sized pieces are exchanged, not resized [FACT-domain]

every return rate, size-exchange rate, ring-size demand distribution, category-level return share, and 'how many returned for size' figure is NOT invented: it is encoded as a measurement method (reason-code attribution, size-exchange tracking, anthropometric/size-sold histograms) tagged [METHOD], a public data source to pull, or an honest [UNKNOWN]
the audience frame (US fashion jewelry, mostly young women ~18-25) is inherited context, not a measured demographic claim; no purchase-rate or ethnicity figure is asserted here
all standard dimensions are stated as the established industry/ISO bands they are; any brand's specific size chart may differ and is confirmed against that brand's own chart before use
exclusions: the category & construction taxonomy itself (kb1_category_construction_taxonomy owns it; this KB consumes it)
shape/motif/style-family aesthetics and shape-to-conversion reasoning (kb2_shape_motif_style_systems owns those)

base-metal and finish materials science, nickel chemistry beyond the return link, and plating durability tests (the materials specialist owns those; this KB only carries the fit/return-relevant edges)
the actual assortment pick, SKU-count, and launch-set-of-six decision (the assortment specialist owns it; this KB hands it a return-risk ranking and size-range requirements)
unit economics of reverse logistics beyond the sizing/exchange driver, CAC/LTV, and pricing (the economics specialist owns those)
asserting any measured return rate, size-exchange percentage, or ring-size demand distribution as fact

competency_questions.question: What are the standard ring sizing systems and how do they convert, and why is the increment size the unit of fit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RING_SIZING_SYSTEMS names US numeric sizing, ISO 8653 inside-circumference-in-mm, and UK/EU/JP systems as [FACT], states ~2.55mm circumference / ~0.81mm diameter per full US size and half-size increments, and gives the conversion basis so a size can be mapped across systems

competency_questions.question: How does band width change the effective fit of a ring at a given nominal size?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RING_WIDTH_FIT_EFFECT states that wider bands fit tighter at the same nominal size (size up ~half size for wide bands), distinguishes knuckle vs base circumference, and explains comfort-fit (domed interior) as fitting ~half size larger

competency_questions.question: What are the standard necklace/chain length bands and anklet/bracelet lengths, and which are effectively one-size?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NECKLACE_CHAIN_LENGTHS lists collar/choker/princess/matinee/opera/rope bands in inches [FACT], names princess ~18 in as the common default, and notes extender chains convert a fixed length into an adjustable range

competency_questions.question: What are the standard hoop diameters and earring post/wire gauges, and which are governed by piercing-standard gauges?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HOOP_DIAMETER_POST_GAUGE states hoop diameter bands (small <20mm, medium ~30-50mm, large >50mm), standard post gauge ~20-21 ga (~0.71-0.81mm), and standard lobe piercing 20 ga / 18 ga [FACT], noting studs/posts are effectively one-size

competency_questions.question: How are bracelets and bangles sized, and why is a bangle's fixed inner diameter a hard-fit dimension while a clasp bracelet is adjustable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BRACELET_BANGLE_SIZING states standard bracelet length ~7-7.5 in, bangle inner diameter bands (~60-70mm), the hand-through constraint for rigid bangles, and that clasp/extender bracelets are adjustable while rigid bangles are a fixed-fit dimension

competency_questions.question: Why can a plated ring not simply be resized, and what does that force for the returns model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLATING_DIMENSIONAL_EFFECT states that plating is a micron-scale surface layer negligible for fit but that resizing abrades/cracks it and forces re-plating, so plated sized pieces are exchanged (new size) not resized, unlike solid metal

competency_questions.question: Which construction choices remove the sizing dimension entirely (adjustable / one-size), and how?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADJUSTABLE_ONE_SIZE_CONSTRUCTIONS names open/adjustable rings, cuffs, slider/bolo and extender chains, and adjustable anklets as constructions that convert a sized item into a fit-tolerant range, and states the tradeoff (fit range gained vs security/premium-feel lost)

competency_questions.question: Which categories carry no meaningful fit dimension at all, so sizing cannot drive their returns?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIZELESS_CATEGORIES identifies studs, pendants on adjustable/standard chains, and charms as categories with no wearer-specific fit dimension, so their return drivers are expectation/quality/allergy, not size

competency_questions.question: What is the return-driver taxonomy for fashion jewelry, and how is the sizing-driven share measured rather than guessed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETURNS_DRIVER_TAXONOMY enumerates the return-reason categories (size/fit, expectation/appearance mismatch, quality/tarnish, allergy/skin reaction, damaged/wrong item) and SIZING_RETURN_LINK gives the reason-code + size-exchange attribution method to measure the sizing share [METHOD], with the rate itself [UNKNOWN]

competency_questions.question: Why are pierced-earring and allergy returns handled differently from size returns?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HYGIENE_RETURN_CONSTRAINT states pierced earrings are commonly final-sale for hygiene reasons (retailer policy norm), and NICKEL_ALLERGY_RETURN ties skin-contact allergy returns to nickel release (EN1811 0.5 ug/cm2/week [FACT]) and hypoallergenic post choice, both distinct from a fit/size cause

competency_questions.question: How is ring-size (and length) demand distribution estimated to set a stocked size range without inventing it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIZE_DISTRIBUTION_METHOD gives the method to estimate size demand (public anthropometric hand/finger data, own size-sold histograms once selling, supplier size-run defaults) tagged [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN], and states how a too-narrow stocked range itself generates size returns

competency_questions.question: Which product-detail-page tools measurably cut sizing-driven returns before purchase?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIZE_GUIDE_UX_METHOD names printable ring sizers / string-wrap method, to-scale hoop-diameter and chain-length visuals, and length-on-model guides as pre-purchase fit tools, and frames measuring their effect via a before/after size-return-rate test [METHOD]

competency_questions.question: Which categories structurally minimize sizing-driven returns, and how is that ranking justified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETURN_MINIMIZING_RANKING ranks categories by sizing-return risk (sizeless studs/pendants and adjustable pieces lowest; fixed-length chains low; bracelets medium; rings highest) with the mechanism for each rank stated, tagged [METHOD] for the ordering and [FACT] for the fit-dimension basis

competency_questions.question: What does the sizing/fit/returns work hand to the assortment decision, and what stays out of scope?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORM_SIZING_HANDOFF delivers the return-risk ranking, the required stocked size ranges, and the size-guide requirement per candidate category, stopping before the assortment pick and the reverse-logistics P&L, and HONESTY_LEDGER separates the [FACT] standards from the [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] return figures

glossary.definition: The US ring sizing system is numeric (roughly sizes 3-13 with half sizes) where each full size adds ~2.55mm of inside circumference (~0.81mm inside diameter); ISO 8653 defines ring size directly as the inside circumference in millimetres (e.g. a ~51.9mm circumference is US ~6). UK/Ireland use a letter system (A-Z), and EU/JP systems use circumference-derived numbers; all convert through inside circumference [FACT-standard].

A wider band and a comfort-fit (domed interior) band both occupy more of the finger and slide over the knuckle less easily, so at the same nominal size they wear tighter; the practical rule is to size up ~half a size for wide (>~6mm) or comfort-fit bands. Fit is set at the knuckle (largest cross-section) not just the base of the finger.

Standard necklace lengths by name: collar ~12-14 in, choker ~14-16 in, princess ~17-19 in (the common default, sits at the collarbone), matinee ~20-24 in, opera ~28-36 in, rope ~36 in+; anklets ~9-10 in; standard bracelet ~7-7.5 in. An extender chain converts a single fixed length into an adjustable range [FACT-industry].

Wire thickness for earring posts and hoops, measured in gauge (higher number = thinner): a standard earring post is ~20-21 ga (~0.71-0.81mm); a standard lobe piercing accepts ~20 ga (~0.8mm) or ~18 ga (~1.0mm). A post thicker than the wearer's piercing will not pass, making gauge a compatibility (not comfort) dimension [FACT].

Hoop earring outside diameter classed roughly as small (<~20mm, hugging/huggie), medium (~30-50mm), and large/statement (>~50mm). Diameter is an aesthetic/scale choice, not a wearer-fit dimension, so hoops carry no per-person sizing the way rings do [FACT-industry convention].

glossary.term: bangle inner diameter vs clasp bracelet
glossary.definition: A rigid bangle must pass over the hand, so its fixed inner diameter (standard bands ~60-70mm, sized S/M/L or by oval hand-through) is a hard-fit dimension; a clasp or extender chain bracelet adjusts to wrist circumference and is fit-tolerant. Bangles therefore carry sizing risk that clasp bracelets largely remove.

The practical fit granularity of a ring is the half-size step (~1.27mm circumference); casting/forming tolerance and the micron-scale plating layer are small relative to that step, so the dominant fit variable is the chosen nominal size, not manufacturing spread. Half sizes are the standard resolution offered.

Electroplated gold/rhodium is a surface layer typically <~2.5um (vermeil >=2.5um over sterling per FTC 16 CFR 23); its thickness is negligible for fit, but bending/cutting a plated ring to resize it cracks and abrades the plating and exposes base metal, forcing full re-plating. Plated sized pieces are therefore exchanged for a new size, not resized [FACT-domain].

A return whose stated reason is fit/size (too big / too small / didn't fit) as opposed to appearance-mismatch, quality/tarnish, allergy, or damage. Its share is measured by tagging each return with a reason code and by tracking size-exchange requests, not assumed; the actual rate is [UNKNOWN] until measured [METHOD].

A category with no wearer-specific fit dimension — stud earrings, pendants on a standard/adjustable chain, charms — so size cannot be a return driver for it and its returns come from expectation, quality, or allergy instead. Sizeless and adjustable categories are the structural way to minimize sizing-driven returns [METHOD].

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for jewel_form_sizing_fit_returns work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Accept kb1's category & construction taxonomy as input and partition it by whether a category carries a wearer-specific fit dimension: SIZED (rings/bands by finger size, rigid bangles by hand-through inner diameter), LENGTH-CHOICE (necklaces/chains, anklets, clasp bracelets — a preference length, adjustable via extender), and SIZELESS (stud earrings, hoops, pendants on standard chains, charms — scale is aesthetic, not per-person). This partition is the spine of the whole KB: everything downstream (fit standards, tolerance, the returns link, the risk ranking) is organized by which bucket a category falls in. No return numbers are asserted here; this only classifies where sizing risk can and cannot originate.

included: the sized / length-choice / sizeless partition of the inherited taxonomy
the principle that sizing risk originates only in fit dimensions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the inherited taxonomy or a construction changes a category's fit bucket

pros.claim: Partitioning categories by fit dimension up front makes every downstream sizing and return claim attach to the right bucket instead of treating all jewelry as uniformly sized
pros.example: placing studs in SIZELESS immediately explains why they cannot generate a size return, while rings in SIZED carry the full half-size risk

cons.claim: A three-bucket partition hides borderline cases (a fixed-length choker, a non-adjustable ring stack) that behave between buckets
cons.example: a rigid choker is length-choice yet not adjustable, so it carries more fit risk than a clasp necklace in the same bucket

failure_modes: treating every category as sized and over-attributing size returns
mislabeling a rigid bangle as length-choice/adjustable when it is a hard-fit dimension
acceptance_tests: the sized / length-choice / sizeless partition is stated with each inherited category assigned to a bucket and the rule that sizing risk originates only in fit dimensions
revisit_triggers: kb1 republishes or extends the category taxonomy
a new construction (e.g. adjustable ring) moves a category between buckets

nodes.definition: Establish the ring sizing standards and their conversion basis [FACT]: the US system is numeric (~sizes 3-13 with half sizes) where each full size adds ~2.55mm inside circumference (~0.81mm inside diameter); ISO 8653 defines size directly as the inside circumference in millimetres (a ~51.9mm circumference is US ~6, EU ~52, UK ~L/M); UK/Ireland use a letter system (A-Z, half letters); Japan/China use their own circumference-derived numbers. All systems convert through inside circumference, so a size chart or a mm measurement is the interoperable anchor. This node fixes the vocabulary and the increment; RING_WIDTH_FIT_EFFECT and FIT_TOLERANCE_MODEL then explain how width and tolerance modulate the fit at a given nominal size. Any specific brand chart is confirmed against that brand, since minor variations exist.

included: US numeric, ISO 8653 mm-circumference, UK letter and EU/JP systems
the ~2.55mm-circumference / ~0.81mm-diameter per full US size increment
inside circumference as the conversion anchor

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a ring size standard or adopted chart changes

pros.claim: Anchoring every ring size to inside circumference in mm gives one interoperable unit across US/UK/EU/JP charts
pros.example: a customer's 52mm measurement maps to US ~6 / UK ~L / EU 52 without ambiguity

cons.claim: Stating a single conversion glosses over small per-brand chart differences and rounding at half sizes
cons.example: one brand's 'size 6' may be 51.8mm and another's 52.1mm, a difference that matters near a knuckle

failure_modes: publishing a US-only size chart and forcing international customers to guess
confusing inside diameter with inside circumference in a conversion
acceptance_tests: US numeric, ISO 8653 mm-circumference, UK letter and EU/JP systems are stated with the ~2.55mm-circumference per full US size increment and inside circumference as the conversion anchor
revisit_triggers: a target-market chart standard (e.g. a specific retailer) is adopted
an ISO 8653 revision changes the size definition
a brand size chart is found to deviate from the standard increment

nodes.definition: State the standard necklace/chain length bands [FACT-industry] and their fit character: collar ~12-14 in, choker ~14-16 in, princess ~17-19 in (the common default, sits at/just below the collarbone), matinee ~20-24 in, opera ~28-36 in, rope ~36 in+; anklets ~9-10 in; standard bracelet ~7-7.5 in. Length is a preference/proportion choice rather than a hard per-person fit, and an extender chain (typically +1 to +3 in) converts a single fixed length into an adjustable range that absorbs most length dissatisfaction. Because most chains are length-choice and easily made adjustable, they sit lower on the sizing-return-risk ladder than rings; the exception is a rigid choker or a fixed non-extendable length, which behaves closer to a sized item.

included: the named length bands in inches
princess ~18 in as the default
the extender chain as the adjustability lever

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a hero length or a length-return signal changes the standard used

pros.claim: Naming the length bands and the extender lever lets a chain be offered as effectively adjustable, cutting length dissatisfaction
pros.example: an 18 in princess chain with a 2 in extender covers ~16-18 in and satisfies both choker-leaning and standard wearers

cons.claim: Length is partly a body/proportion and styling preference, so a nominal band cannot guarantee the look the buyer imagined
cons.example: an 18 in chain reads as a choker on a larger neck and mid-chest on a smaller frame, a fit surprise no chart fully prevents

failure_modes: selling a fixed length with no extender and absorbing avoidable length returns
labeling a length band without a to-scale or on-model reference so buyers misjudge drop
acceptance_tests: the collar/choker/princess/matinee/opera/rope bands and anklet/bracelet lengths are stated in inches with the extender chain named as the adjustability lever
revisit_triggers: a target length becomes the hero SKU and needs a firm chart
size-return data shows a specific length driving length returns

nodes.definition: State the earring dimensional standards [FACT]: hoop outside diameter bands — small (<~20mm, huggie/hugging), medium (~30-50mm), large/statement (>~50mm) — where diameter is an aesthetic/scale choice, not a wearer-fit dimension; and post/wire gauge, where a standard earring post is ~20-21 ga (~0.71-0.81mm) and a standard lobe piercing accepts ~20 ga (~0.8mm) or ~18 ga (~1.0mm). Gauge is a compatibility dimension: a post thicker than the wearer's piercing will not pass, so a heavier-gauge post is a friction point for standard 20 ga piercings. Studs and posts are effectively one-size (SIZELESS bucket); hoop diameter is a look, not a fit, so earrings carry no per-person sizing the way rings do — their returns come from appearance, hygiene, or allergy, not fit.

included: hoop diameter bands
standard post/wire gauge ~20-21 ga and piercing 20/18 ga
post gauge as a compatibility (not comfort) dimension

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a post gauge, piercing standard, or hoop convention changes

pros.claim: Fixing standard 20-21 ga posts keeps earrings compatible with the standard lobe piercing and removes a silent friction return
pros.example: a post at 20 ga passes a standard piercing, whereas an 18 ga post can be rejected as too thick

cons.claim: Diameter and gauge alone do not capture weight/leverage comfort, which also drives earring dissatisfaction
cons.example: a large-diameter hoop within spec can still be rejected as too heavy for the lobe

failure_modes: shipping a heavier-than-standard post gauge that will not pass a common piercing
treating hoop diameter as a fit dimension and adding needless size variants
acceptance_tests: the hoop diameter bands, the standard ~20-21 ga post gauge, and standard 20/18 ga piercing are stated with post gauge framed as a compatibility dimension and earrings placed in the sizeless bucket
revisit_triggers: a heavier-gauge or thicker post style is proposed
an earring-weight comfort issue surfaces in returns

nodes.definition: State bracelet and bangle sizing and split them by fit character [FACT]: a clasp/chain bracelet is length-choice (standard ~7-7.5 in, adjustable via extender or multiple clasp rings) and fit-tolerant; a rigid bangle must pass over the hand, so its fixed inner diameter (standard bands roughly 60-70mm, offered S/M/L or as an oval to match the hand-through dimension) is a hard-fit dimension. The controlling measurement for a bangle is the widest hand circumference (thumb tucked), not the wrist, since the bangle has to clear the knuckles. Cuffs sit between: an open cuff with a gap is adjustable within a range. This node makes bracelets mostly low-risk (adjustable) but flags rigid bangles as a genuine sizing-return category alongside rings.

included: standard bracelet ~7-7.5 in and adjustability
bangle inner-diameter bands and the hand-through constraint
cuffs as adjustable-within-range

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rigid-bangle SKU or a bangle-fit signal changes the sizing need

pros.claim: Separating clasp bracelets from rigid bangles keeps most bracelets low-risk while correctly flagging bangles as a hard-fit sizing category
pros.example: a clasp bracelet with a 1 in extender fits a wide wrist range, whereas a fixed 65mm bangle fails anyone whose hand won't pass

cons.claim: Bangle fit depends on hand-through not wrist, a measurement most buyers don't know how to take, so bangle sizing stays error-prone even with bands
cons.example: a buyer measures wrist ~15cm and orders a bangle that won't clear their knuckles

failure_modes: sizing a bangle to wrist circumference instead of hand-through and shipping an unwearable piece
treating a rigid bangle as adjustable and skipping a size range
acceptance_tests: standard bracelet length, bangle inner-diameter bands with the hand-through constraint, and the clasp-vs-rigid fit split are stated
revisit_triggers: a rigid bangle is proposed as a launch SKU
a bangle size-return signal appears
an oval/adjustable bangle construction is considered

nodes.definition: Explain how band geometry modulates the fit of a ring at a given nominal size [FACT]: a wider band (>~6mm) and a comfort-fit (domed-interior) band both wear tighter than a thin flat band of the same nominal size, because they contact more of the finger and clear the knuckle less easily; the standard rule is to size up ~half a size for wide or comfort-fit bands. Fit is governed at the knuckle (the largest cross-section the ring must pass), not just the base of the finger, so a ring must be loose enough to go on and snug enough to stay. This is why a single 'finger size' underdetermines fit and why width must be published alongside size — a mismatch here is a common, avoidable driver of ring size returns that a size chart alone does not fix.

included: wide/comfort-fit bands wearing tighter and the size-up-half rule
knuckle vs base circumference
publishing band width alongside size

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a band-width offering or a width-linked return signal changes

pros.claim: Publishing width and the size-up rule alongside nominal size closes a fit gap a size chart alone leaves open
pros.example: a 8mm comfort-fit band listed with 'size up half' prevents the tight-at-knuckle return a bare 'size 7' would cause

cons.claim: The half-size-up rule is a heuristic that varies with individual knuckle-to-base ratio, so it reduces but does not eliminate fit surprises
cons.example: a wearer with a large knuckle and slim base finds even the adjusted size spins

failure_modes: listing only a nominal size for a wide band and absorbing tight-fit returns
sizing to base-of-finger circumference so the ring won't pass the knuckle
acceptance_tests: the wide/comfort-fit-fits-tighter effect, the size-up-half rule, and knuckle-governed fit are stated with the instruction to publish band width alongside size
revisit_triggers: a wide or comfort-fit band becomes a hero SKU
ring size-return data implicates band width

nodes.definition: Define the fit-tolerance model that sets the practical resolution of ring fit [FACT/METHOD]: the fit unit is the half-size step (~1.27mm inside circumference; a full US size ~2.55mm), and this dwarfs the other dimensional variances — casting/forming tolerance and the micron-scale plating layer are each an order of magnitude smaller than a half size — so the dominant fit variable is the nominal size chosen by the buyer, not the manufacturing spread. The practical consequences: offer half sizes for rings (whole-size-only stocking forces buyers to round and mis-fit); hold a consistent internal tolerance so a labeled size is repeatable across a plating batch; and recognize that once a buyer has picked the right nominal size, tolerance is not the bottleneck — measurement and band-width choice are. This node is the quantitative bridge from the size standards to the returns link.

included: the half-size step (~1.27mm) as the fit unit
casting and plating variance being small vs a half size
offering half sizes and holding internal tolerance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a tolerance measurement or a half-size stocking decision changes

pros.claim: Framing the half-size step as the fit unit shows that offering half sizes and consistent tolerance solves most controllable fit error
pros.example: a buyer between whole sizes who can pick a half size avoids the forced round-up that causes a loose-ring return

cons.claim: Half-size granularity plus tolerance still cannot correct a buyer who measured wrong or ignored the width rule
cons.example: a correct half-size offering does not help a customer who guessed their size from a friend's ring

failure_modes: stocking whole sizes only and forcing mis-fit rounding
letting internal tolerance drift across plating batches so a labeled size becomes inconsistent
acceptance_tests: the ~1.27mm half-size fit unit, the smallness of casting/plating variance relative to it, and the offer-half-sizes / hold-tolerance consequences are stated
revisit_triggers: a supplier's casting tolerance is measured off-spec
a decision to stock whole-sizes-only is proposed
a plating batch shifts labeled-size consistency

nodes.definition: Carry the plating-specific dimensional and durability facts that distinguish plated from solid pieces [FACT-domain]: an electroplated gold/rhodium layer is thin (typically <~2.5um; vermeil is defined as >=10k gold plating >=2.5um over sterling per FTC 16 CFR 23), so its contribution to a ring's inside diameter is negligible for fit — plating does not meaningfully change the size. The decisive fact is mechanical, not dimensional: resizing a plated ring (cutting, stretching, soldering) abrades and cracks the surface layer and exposes the base metal, so a plated ring effectively cannot be locally resized without full re-plating. This forces the returns model for sized plated pieces toward exchange-for-a-new-size rather than in-house resize, and it raises the value of getting the size right the first time (size guides, half sizes, adjustable constructions) far above where it sits for solid metal.

included: plating thickness negligible for fit
resizing cracks/abrades plating and forces re-plating
the shift from resize to exchange for plated sized pieces
excluded: the reverse-logistics economics of that exchange (RESIZING_EXCHANGE_ECONOMICS)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a plating spec, resize capability, or FTC definition changes

pros.claim: Naming plating fragility explains why 'just resize it' is not available for plated rings and why first-time fit accuracy is disproportionately valuable
pros.example: a plated ring returned one size off cannot be bench-resized like a solid gold ring; it must be swapped, so a size guide pays back more here

cons.claim: The no-resize rule is a strong general truth but some thick-plated or heavily-plated pieces tolerate minor adjustment, so it is a near-absolute not an absolute
cons.example: a very lightly resized shank might be touched up rather than fully re-plated in rare cases

failure_modes: promising ring resizing on plated pieces and then damaging the finish
assuming plating thickness affects fit and over-correcting the size
acceptance_tests: plating thickness negligible for fit, resizing forcing re-plating, and the resulting exchange-not-resize model for plated sized pieces are stated with the FTC vermeil basis
revisit_triggers: a heavier plating spec or a resize-capable finish is introduced
a supplier offers plated-piece resizing
the FTC plating definitions are revised

nodes.definition: Catalogue the constructions that convert a sized item into a fit-tolerant one and thereby remove sizing-return risk [METHOD/FACT]: open/adjustable rings (a gap that flexes across ~2-3 sizes), open cuffs (adjustable within a range), slider/bolo and lariat chains (continuously adjustable length), extender chains on necklaces/bracelets/anklets (+1 to +3 in), and adjustable/oval bangles. Each trades a precise custom fit for a tolerant range: the gain is one SKU covering many wearers, no size-range stocking, and near-elimination of size returns; the cost is a slightly less secure or less premium feel and, for open rings, a risk of the wearer over-flexing and fatiguing the metal (a plating-crack risk on plated pieces). For a plated launch minimizing size returns, adjustable constructions are the single most powerful lever after choosing sizeless categories.

included: adjustable rings, cuffs, slider/lariat and extender chains, oval/adjustable bangles
the one-SKU-covers-many-wearers gain and the security/feel/fatigue cost

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an adjustable construction choice or a plating-fatigue signal changes

pros.claim: Adjustable constructions collapse a size range into one SKU and near-eliminate size returns without going fully sizeless
pros.example: an open adjustable ring covering ~sizes 6-8 as one SKU removes both the stocking problem and most size returns

cons.claim: Adjustability trades away secure/premium fit and, on plated open rings, invites over-flexing that cracks the plating
cons.example: a customer repeatedly opening an adjustable plated ring fatigues the shank and chips the finish, converting a size win into a quality return

failure_modes: over-using open plated rings that customers over-flex and crack
assuming adjustable = infinite fit and dropping a needed size variant for a rigid piece
acceptance_tests: the adjustable ring/cuff/slider/extender/oval-bangle constructions, the one-SKU-covers-many gain, and the security/feel/plating-fatigue cost are stated
revisit_triggers: an adjustable construction is chosen for a hero SKU
a plating-fatigue return signal appears on open pieces
a premium-feel positioning conflicts with adjustability

nodes.definition: Identify the categories that carry no wearer-specific fit dimension at all, so sizing structurally cannot drive their returns [METHOD/FACT]: stud earrings and posts (one-size; only gauge compatibility matters), pendants/necklaces sold on a standard or adjustable chain (length is a preference, not a fit), charms and pendant components, and hoops (diameter is a look, not a fit). For these categories the return drivers are appearance/expectation mismatch, quality/tarnish, hygiene, and allergy — never size — which makes them the structurally lowest sizing-return-risk categories a launch can pick. This node, together with ADJUSTABLE_ONE_SIZE_CONSTRUCTIONS, defines the two routes to a low-size-return assortment: choose sizeless categories, or make a sized category adjustable.

included: studs, pendants on chains, charms, hoops as sizeless
size cannot be their return driver
sizeless as one of the two low-return routes
excluded: the non-size return drivers they still face (RETURNS_DRIVER_TAXONOMY, NICKEL_ALLERGY_RETURN)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a category's fit character or its non-size return mix changes

pros.claim: Naming the sizeless categories gives a launch a structural way to zero out size returns by category choice alone
pros.example: a stud + pendant + hoop assortment cannot generate a single size return because none carries a fit dimension

cons.claim: Sizeless does not mean return-free: these categories still face appearance, quality, hygiene and allergy returns, which can be higher than a well-sized ring
cons.example: a pendant returned because it looked smaller than the photo shows sizeless is not returnless

failure_modes: treating sizeless as return-proof and neglecting appearance/quality/allergy drivers
misclassifying a rigid choker or bangle as sizeless
acceptance_tests: studs, pendants on chains, charms and hoops are identified as sizeless with size ruled out as a return driver and the non-size drivers noted
revisit_triggers: a category's construction changes its fit character
appearance/quality returns on a sizeless category spike

nodes.definition: Enumerate the return-reason categories for fashion/plated jewelry so returns can be attributed rather than lumped [FACT-taxonomy / METHOD]: (1) size/fit — too big, too small, won't fit/pass; (2) appearance/expectation mismatch — colour, scale, or look differs from the photo; (3) quality/durability — tarnish, plating wear, clasp/stone failure; (4) allergy/skin reaction — redness/irritation on skin contact; (5) damaged/defective/wrong item. Only category (1) is sizing-driven; the others are not fixed by a better size chart. Reason (3) is finish-specific for plated goods (tarnish/wear) and reason (4) links to base-metal/nickel. Establishing this taxonomy is the precondition for measuring the sizing share of returns honestly: without reason codes, 'size returns' is a guess.

included: the five return-reason categories
isolating size/fit as the only sizing-driven reason
reason codes as the precondition for measurement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the return-reason code taxonomy changes

pros.claim: A clean reason taxonomy separates the size-fixable returns from the ones a size guide cannot touch, preventing misattribution
pros.example: tagging a tarnish return as quality (3) not size (1) stops a size guide from being credited with a fix it cannot make

cons.claim: Customer-stated reasons are noisy and sometimes strategic, so even coded reasons carry misattribution error
cons.example: a buyer with remorse may select 'didn't fit' as the least-friction reason, inflating the size bucket

failure_modes: lumping all returns as one bucket so sizing cannot be isolated
trusting free-text reasons without a coded taxonomy
acceptance_tests: the five return-reason categories are enumerated with size/fit isolated as the only sizing-driven reason and reason codes named as the measurement precondition
revisit_triggers: the return-reason code set is revised
a new failure mode (e.g. plating wear pattern) needs its own code

nodes.definition: Define the causal link and the honest way to measure it [METHOD; rate UNKNOWN]: sized categories (rings, rigid bangles) have a structurally higher size-return exposure than length-choice or sizeless categories, because only they can be 'the wrong size on arrival.' The sizing-driven share is measured, not assumed, by (a) tagging each return with the reason code (from RETURNS_DRIVER_TAXONOMY), (b) tracking size-exchange requests (a size return that comes back as a re-order of the same style in another size is unambiguously sizing-driven), and (c) computing a per-category size-return rate = size-coded returns / units sold, segmented by category and by whether the piece was fixed-size vs adjustable. The absolute rates are [UNKNOWN] until the store measures them; general priors (rings highest, sizeless ~zero) set direction only. This node is the quantitative hinge from fit standards to the risk ranking.

included: sized categories carrying higher size-return exposure
reason-code + size-exchange + per-category-rate measurement method
absolute rates as [UNKNOWN], direction only from priors

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured return data or a tracking mechanism changes the size-return estimate

pros.claim: A defined size-return rate per category, measured from reason codes and size-exchanges, replaces guessed return numbers with an auditable method
pros.example: counting same-style-different-size re-orders isolates unambiguous sizing returns the store can actually track

cons.claim: Until the store has volume, per-category size-return rates are [UNKNOWN] and only the direction (rings > bracelets > sizeless) is defensible
cons.example: a new launch cannot state its ring size-return rate; it can only rank rings as highest-risk a priori

failure_modes: quoting a fabricated size-return percentage instead of the measured/UNKNOWN one
attributing appearance or quality returns to sizing for lack of reason codes
acceptance_tests: the higher size-return exposure of sized categories, the reason-code + size-exchange + per-category-rate method, and the [UNKNOWN]-until-measured status of absolute rates are stated
revisit_triggers: the store accumulates enough returns to compute per-category size-return rates
a size-exchange tracking mechanism is added
a category's fixed-vs-adjustable mix changes

nodes.definition: Carry the hygiene-return constraint that makes earrings a special case [FACT-policy norm]: pierced earrings are commonly sold final-sale / non-returnable for hygiene reasons, a widespread retailer policy grounded in the fact that a worn earring has contacted a pierced (broken-skin) site. This means an earring's fit/appearance risk cannot be recovered through a return the way a ring's can, so the mitigation shifts entirely to pre-purchase accuracy (clear scale/gauge, to-scale images) and to a returns policy stated plainly at checkout. It also means earring returns are dominated by not-fit reasons (appearance, allergy, defect handled via replacement) rather than size, reinforcing earrings' place among the lowest sizing-return-risk categories — but with a distinct, non-recoverable hygiene exposure the ranking must note. This is a policy/commercial norm, not a single statute; the specific policy is set by the seller.

included: pierced earrings commonly final-sale for hygiene
mitigation shifting to pre-purchase accuracy and clear policy
earring returns dominated by non-size reasons

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the earring hygiene-return policy or a marketplace requirement changes

pros.claim: Flagging the hygiene final-sale norm reframes earring risk as pre-purchase accuracy plus clear policy, not post-purchase recovery
pros.example: stating final-sale-for-hygiene at checkout with to-scale images pre-empts disputes a return would otherwise absorb

cons.claim: Final-sale on earrings can raise appearance-mismatch friction and chargebacks, so the hygiene policy trades a return channel for a support/dispute channel
cons.example: a buyer who finds a hoop smaller than expected cannot return it and disputes the charge instead

failure_modes: accepting worn-earring returns and creating a hygiene/liability problem
hiding the final-sale policy so buyers feel misled and dispute
acceptance_tests: the pierced-earring final-sale hygiene norm, the shift to pre-purchase accuracy and clear checkout policy, and the non-size dominance of earring returns are stated as a seller-set policy norm not a statute
revisit_triggers: the store's earring return policy is set or changed
a marketplace requires a specific hygiene-return stance
earring dispute/chargeback rates rise

nodes.definition: Carry the allergy-driven return driver and its material link [FACT]: skin-contact irritation (contact dermatitis) is a real return reason for earrings and other skin-contact pieces, most commonly from nickel release; the EU EN1811 standard caps nickel release at 0.5 ug/cm2/week for prolonged skin contact, and posts/base metals that exceed this drive allergy returns and one-star reviews. Because earrings sit in a pierced (broken-skin) site, they are the highest allergy-return category, and the mitigation is a material choice (nickel-safe base metal, hypoallergenic posts such as titanium/surgical-steel/nickel-free) sourced from the materials specialist, not a sizing fix. This is distinct from a fit return: it cannot be reduced by a size guide, only by base-metal and finish selection, and it interacts with the hygiene final-sale norm because an allergy return is often handled as a replacement/refund exception.

included: nickel-release allergy as a return driver
EN1811 0.5 ug/cm2/week as the reference limit
hypoallergenic post/base-metal mitigation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a base-metal choice, allergy signal, or nickel regulation changes

pros.claim: Linking allergy returns to nickel release and the EN1811 limit points the fix at base-metal selection rather than a futile sizing change
pros.example: specifying nickel-safe posts under the EN1811 limit reduces earring allergy returns a size guide could never touch

cons.claim: Allergy is partly wearer-specific (some react below the limit; some to other metals), so a compliant post reduces but does not eliminate allergy returns
cons.example: a highly sensitive wearer reacts even to a nickel-safe hypoallergenic post

failure_modes: treating allergy returns as fixable by a size guide
shipping a post above the EN1811 nickel-release limit into a pierced site
acceptance_tests: nickel-release allergy as a return driver, the EN1811 0.5 ug/cm2/week reference, and hypoallergenic base-metal mitigation (not a sizing fix) are stated
revisit_triggers: a base-metal or post material is changed
an allergy-return signal rises
the EN1811 limit or a market nickel regulation changes

nodes.definition: Give the honest method to set a stocked size range without inventing a demand distribution [METHOD; distribution UNKNOWN]: a too-narrow ring-size range is itself a size-return generator (buyers forced to the nearest stocked size), while a too-wide range strands inventory capital in slow sizes. The size distribution is estimated, not assumed, from (a) public anthropometric finger/hand data as a starting prior, (b) supplier/industry default size runs (the sizes a manufacturer stocks reflect aggregate demand), and (c) the store's own size-sold histogram once it has volume — the authoritative source, which supersedes the priors. The same logic applies to necklace lengths (offer the common princess default plus an extender rather than many fixed lengths) and bangle S/M/L. No specific size-share percentage is asserted; the method yields a defensible range and flags the distribution as [UNKNOWN] until the store's own sales measure it.

included: too-narrow range as a return generator vs too-wide as capital drag
anthropometric prior + supplier default + own size-sold histogram method
distribution as [UNKNOWN] until measured

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an own-sales size histogram or supplier default run changes the range

pros.claim: A method that layers a public prior, supplier defaults, and own sales data sets a stocked range without inventing a size distribution
pros.example: starting from a supplier's standard size run and refining with the store's size-sold histogram avoids both stockout and dead-size capital

cons.claim: Until the store has its own sales, the range rests on generic priors that may not match its actual audience, keeping the distribution [UNKNOWN]
cons.example: a store skewed to a specific audience may find its real size peak differs from the anthropometric prior

failure_modes: stocking a too-narrow range and manufacturing avoidable size returns
asserting a specific size-share percentage the store has not measured
acceptance_tests: the narrow-vs-wide range tradeoff, the anthropometric-prior + supplier-default + own-histogram method, and the [UNKNOWN]-until-measured distribution are stated
revisit_triggers: the store accumulates a size-sold histogram
a supplier's default size run changes
a stockout or dead-size signal appears in a specific size

nodes.definition: Specify the product-detail-page fit tools that cut sizing-driven returns before purchase and how to measure their effect [METHOD]: a printable ring sizer strip and the string/paper-wrap-and-measure method (mapped to the mm-circumference chart), an existing-ring measurement guide, to-scale hoop-diameter and chain-length reference images (a ruler or coin for scale, or overlay on a model), a necklace length-on-model visual, and an explicit band-width / size-up note for wide rings. Each tool attacks the measurement-error and expectation-mismatch sources of size and appearance returns. Their impact is not assumed but measured with a before/after (or A/B) size-coded-return-rate test: introduce the tool, hold everything else, and read the change in size-coded returns for that category. The tools are cheapest and highest-leverage exactly where resize is unavailable (plated rings), tying this node back to the plating constraint.

included: ring sizer / string method, to-scale hoop & chain visuals, length-on-model, band-width note
before/after or A/B size-return-rate measurement of the tools

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a PDP fit tool or its measured effect changes

pros.claim: Pre-purchase fit tools attack the measurement-error and expectation sources of returns and their effect is directly A/B-measurable
pros.example: adding a printable ring sizer and reading the size-coded return rate before vs after quantifies the tool's payback

cons.claim: Fit tools rely on buyers actually using them and measuring correctly, so their return-cut is real but partial and self-selected
cons.example: a buyer who ignores the string-method guide still guesses their size and returns it

failure_modes: shipping a size chart with no to-scale reference so buyers misjudge scale
claiming a return reduction from a tool without an A/B or before/after measurement
acceptance_tests: the ring-sizer/string, to-scale hoop & chain visuals, length-on-model and band-width tools are named with a before/after or A/B size-return-rate measurement method
revisit_triggers: a fit tool is added or changed on the PDP
an A/B test on a fit tool completes
a category's size-coded return rate shifts

nodes.definition: Synthesize the KB's headline decision output [METHOD]: rank candidate categories by structural sizing-return risk so a launch can bias toward low-risk categories. Ordering (direction is defensible from fit-dimension facts; absolute rates [UNKNOWN]): LOWEST — sizeless categories (studs, pendants on adjustable chains, hoops, charms) which carry no fit dimension; then adjustable-construction pieces (open/adjustable rings, cuffs, slider chains, extendable necklaces/bracelets) which collapse a size range into one tolerant SKU; then fixed-length chains/clasp bracelets (length-choice, mostly satisfiable with an extender); MEDIUM — rigid bangles (hand-through hard-fit); HIGHEST — fixed-size rings, where a wrong nominal size is unrecoverable-by-resize on plated goods. The ranking is a bias, not a ban: a ring can still launch if paired with half sizes, a size guide, and an exchange path. This directly answers the owner's 'which categories minimize sizing-driven returns' and feeds the assortment specialist.

included: the sizeless < adjustable < fixed-length < bangle < ring risk ordering
the mechanism for each rank
ranking as a bias not a ban, with mitigations for rings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured return rates or a construction change re-orders the ranking

pros.claim: A category risk ranking gives the assortment a defensible, fact-anchored bias toward low-size-return categories directly answering the owner's question
pros.example: leading a launch with studs, pendants and adjustable rings minimizes size returns by construction while still allowing a hero ring with mitigations

cons.claim: The ranking orders risk direction but not magnitude, so it cannot say how much lower one category is until the store measures rates
cons.example: rings rank highest-risk but the actual gap to bangles is [UNKNOWN] pre-launch

failure_modes: reading the ranking as a ban on rings rather than a bias plus mitigations
presenting the ordering with invented absolute return rates
acceptance_tests: the sizeless < adjustable < fixed-length < bangle < ring ordering with each rank's mechanism is stated as a bias-not-ban, with absolute rates flagged [UNKNOWN]
revisit_triggers: measured per-category size-return rates arrive and re-order or confirm the ranking
a new construction changes a category's fit character
the assortment requests a re-weighting

nodes.definition: Model the operational consequence of the plating constraint for sized returns [METHOD]: because a plated ring cannot be bench-resized without re-plating (from PLATING_DIMENSIONAL_EFFECT), a size return is handled as an exchange (ship the correct size, take back the wrong one) or a refund, not an in-house resize. This makes each ring size return a full reverse-logistics event — return shipping, inspection, restocking or write-off of the returned piece (a used plated ring may not be resellable), and a second outbound shipment — which is materially costlier than a length adjustment or a sizeless-item refund. The design levers that cut this cost are upstream: prefer sizeless/adjustable categories, offer half sizes and a size guide to get it right first time, and set a store-credit/exchange-first policy to retain the sale. This node states the flow and its cost drivers; the full unit economics belong to the economics specialist.

included: exchange/refund not resize for plated sized returns
the full reverse-logistics event and its cost drivers
upstream design levers and exchange-first policy
excluded: the full reverse-logistics P&L / CAC (economics specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a resize/resale capability or return policy changes the exchange flow

pros.claim: Framing a plated size return as a full reverse-logistics event, not a cheap resize, exposes why first-time fit and low-size-return categories pay back operationally
pros.example: a ring exchange costs two shipments plus a possibly-unsellable returned piece, dwarfing a sizeless refund's single leg

cons.claim: The economics are directional here; actual per-return cost depends on shipping, restock resale and policy the economics specialist owns
cons.example: whether a returned plated ring is resold or written off swings the cost materially and is not decided in this KB

failure_modes: assuming plated rings can be cheaply resized like solid metal
ignoring that a used returned plated ring may be unsellable and mis-costing the return
acceptance_tests: the exchange/refund-not-resize handling, the full reverse-logistics event and cost drivers, and the upstream levers plus exchange-first policy are stated
revisit_triggers: a resize-capable finish or a resale-of-returns process is introduced
the return/exchange policy changes
the economics specialist supplies reverse-logistics costs

nodes.definition: Enforce the honesty discipline across the KB so the size standards are trusted as facts while every return/size-share number stays a method or an [UNKNOWN]. Solid [FACT] (cited, load-bearing): the ring sizing systems and the ~2.55mm-per-full-size increment (ISO 8653 / industry); the necklace length bands; the hoop-diameter and 20-21 ga post / 20-18 ga piercing standards; the plating-fragility no-resize truth and the FTC vermeil definition; the EN1811 nickel-release limit. Method-or-unknown [METHOD/UNKNOWN]: every size-return rate, size-exchange rate, per-category return share, and ring-size demand distribution (measured via reason codes, size-exchange tracking, and own size-sold histograms — never guessed); the earring hygiene final-sale stance (a seller-set policy norm). The category risk ranking is [METHOD] on the ordering and [FACT] on the fit-dimension basis. This ledger tells a reader exactly which claims are standards to rely on and which are numbers the store must still measure.

included: the [FACT] size/standard anchors vs the [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] return figures
the ranking as method-ordering on a fact basis
the hygiene stance as a policy norm
excluded: the substantive standard content (the other nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a standard is revised or a [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] figure is measured

pros.claim: A single ledger separating cited size standards from unmeasured return figures keeps the KB trustworthy and prevents an [UNKNOWN] rate from being read as a fact
pros.example: tagging the ~2.55mm increment [FACT] but the ring size-return rate [UNKNOWN] tells a reader exactly what to rely on

cons.claim: Heavy tagging frustrates a stakeholder who wants a single size-return number the evidence does not yet support
cons.example: an owner wanting 'the ring return rate' must accept a method and an [UNKNOWN] until the store measures it

failure_modes: promoting an [UNKNOWN] size-return rate to a quoted fact
hardening a generic size-demand prior into a claimed distribution
acceptance_tests: the [FACT] size/standard anchors, the [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] return figures, and the ranking's method-vs-fact split are enumerated
revisit_triggers: a [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] figure is measured and hardened by the store's own data
a cited standard (ISO 8653, EN1811, FTC) is revised

nodes.definition: Compose the segment's hand-off to the assortment and economics specialists and stop cleanly. Deliver per candidate category: (1) its sizing-return-risk rank (from RETURN_MINIMIZING_RANKING); (2) the fit standard and required stocked range if sized (ring half-size range, necklace length + extender, bangle S/M/L, or 'sizeless — none'); (3) the required pre-purchase fit tools (size guide, to-scale imagery, band-width note); and (4) the return-handling implication (plated rings need an exchange-first path; earrings a stated hygiene policy). This KB owns whether a category's form creates or avoids sizing-driven returns and how to measure the effect; it does NOT own the assortment pick, the reverse-logistics P&L, or CAC/pricing. The binding conditions it passes on: bias the launch toward sizeless/adjustable categories, offer half sizes and a size guide for any ring, measure size-coded returns from day one, and never quote an unmeasured size-return rate as fact.

included: per-category rank + required size range + fit tools + return-handling
the clean boundary before the assortment pick and reverse-logistics P&L
the binding conditions passed to the assortment/economics specialists
excluded: the assortment pick and SKU count (assortment specialist)
the reverse-logistics P&L, CAC and pricing (economics specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured rank, a downstream request, or a standard/policy change updates the hand-off

pros.claim: A clean hand-off gives the assortment a per-category risk rank, size range, fit-tool and return-handling spec without overstepping into the pick or the P&L
pros.example: handing over 'rings: highest size-return risk, offer half sizes 5-9 + ring sizer + exchange-first' lets the assortment decide with the fit reality priced in

cons.claim: The hand-off carries risk direction and [UNKNOWN] rates, so the assortment inherits an ordering not measured magnitudes
cons.example: the assortment must weigh rings' highest-risk rank against demand without a measured return rate yet

failure_modes: letting the hand-off drift into making the assortment pick this segment does not own
passing a single invented size-return number instead of the rank plus the [UNKNOWN] flag
acceptance_tests: the per-category rank + size range + fit tools + return-handling, the clean pre-pick/pre-P&L boundary, and the four binding conditions are stated
revisit_triggers: measured size-return data updates a category's rank
the assortment or economics specialist requests a different cut
a fit standard or return policy changes

edges.resolution_rule: prefer a genuinely sizeless category when the design allows it (zero fit dimension); use an adjustable construction only when the category is inherently sized but must launch, since adjustability adds a security/premium-feel and plating-fatigue cost a sizeless piece avoids

conflict_axes.name: sizeless_route_vs_adjustable_route
conflict_axes.description: Two routes minimize size returns — pick a genuinely sizeless category, or make a sized category adjustable — and they compete for the same SKU slots with different feel and inventory implications.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer sizeless where the design allows zero fit dimension; use adjustable only when the category is inherently sized but must launch, accepting its security/feel/plating-fatigue cost

conflict_axes.name: fixed_size_range_vs_adjustable_coverage
conflict_axes.description: Fit coverage can come from stocking a full ring/bangle size range or from an adjustable construction, with opposite inventory and size-return consequences.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: favour adjustable/sizeless to avoid the size-range inventory bet; stock a full range only for forms that cannot be adjustable without losing their character

conflict_axes.name: adjustable_fit_vs_plating_durability
conflict_axes.description: Open/adjustable plated pieces cut size returns but repeated flexing cracks the plating, trading a size return for a quality return.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use adjustable plated pieces only where flex is occasional; for frequently adjusted fits prefer sized-with-guide or sizeless designs

conflict_axes.name: narrow_size_range_vs_capital_in_dead_sizes
conflict_axes.description: A narrow stocked size range strands buyers into mis-fit (size returns) while a wide range strands capital in slow-moving sizes.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set the range from supplier defaults refined by the store's own size-sold histogram; widen only where measured demand or size-returns justify it

conflict_axes.name: first_time_fit_accuracy_vs_return_recovery
conflict_axes.description: Because plated rings cannot be cheaply resized and earrings are final-sale, effort must go to pre-purchase fit accuracy rather than post-purchase return recovery.
poles: rely on a generous return path
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: invest first in size guides, half sizes and to-scale imagery; keep an exchange-first return path but do not lean on it where resize is impossible or hygiene forbids return

conflict_axes.name: measured_size_return_rate_vs_a_priori_direction
conflict_axes.description: The category risk order is defensible a priori from fit-dimension facts, but the magnitudes are unknown until the store measures reason-coded returns.
poles: act on the a-priori ranking now
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: act on the ranking's direction to bias the launch, measure size-coded returns from day one, and update magnitudes as data arrives

conflict_axes.name: band_width_realism_vs_single_size_simplicity
conflict_axes.description: A single 'finger size' is simpler to sell but underdetermines fit for wide/comfort-fit bands, which need a size-up note.
poles: publish width and a size-up rule
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: publish band width and the size-up-half rule for wide/comfort-fit rings; keep a bare nominal size only for thin flat bands

conflict_axes.name: bangle_hand_through_vs_wrist_measure
conflict_axes.description: Buyers measure their wrist, but a rigid bangle must clear the hand, so a wrist-based size fails while a hand-through size fits.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: size rigid bangles by the widest hand-through circumference (thumb tucked) and instruct that measurement explicitly, or offer an adjustable/oval bangle instead

conflict_axes.name: hygiene_final_sale_vs_appearance_dispute_risk
conflict_axes.description: Final-sale on pierced earrings avoids a hygiene/liability problem but converts appearance-mismatch returns into support tickets and chargebacks.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the hygiene final-sale stance but state it plainly at checkout and invest in to-scale imagery so appearance mismatch is pre-empted, not disputed

edge_cases.description: A wide or comfort-fit plated ring is sold at a bare nominal size and arrives too tight at the knuckle, generating a size return that cannot be resized
edge_cases.trigger: a wide/comfort-fit band listed without a width or size-up note
edge_cases.mitigation: publish band width and the size-up-half rule and route any wrong-size ring to an exchange, not a resize

edge_cases.description: A rigid bangle is sized to the buyer's wrist circumference and will not pass over the hand
edge_cases.trigger: a bangle size guide that asks for wrist rather than hand-through measurement
edge_cases.mitigation: instruct the widest hand-through measurement (thumb tucked) or offer an adjustable/oval bangle

edge_cases.description: A store quotes a specific ring size-return percentage it has never measured
edge_cases.trigger: a size-return rate is asserted as fact without reason-code data
edge_cases.mitigation: state the rate as [UNKNOWN] and stand up reason-code + size-exchange tracking to measure it

edge_cases.description: An open/adjustable plated ring is repeatedly flexed by the wearer and the plating cracks, turning a size solution into a quality return
edge_cases.trigger: an adjustable plated ring marketed for frequent resizing
edge_cases.mitigation: reserve adjustable plated pieces for occasional flex; prefer sized-with-guide or sizeless for fits that change often

edge_cases.description: A pierced-earring customer is not told the final-sale hygiene policy and disputes the charge after an appearance mismatch
edge_cases.trigger: a hygiene final-sale policy hidden until after purchase
edge_cases.mitigation: state final-sale-for-hygiene at checkout and provide to-scale imagery so scale is understood pre-purchase

edge_cases.description: The stocked ring-size range is too narrow, forcing buyers to round to the nearest size and manufacturing avoidable size returns
edge_cases.trigger: a whole-sizes-only or truncated size range set from a generic prior
edge_cases.mitigation: offer half sizes and set the range from supplier defaults refined by the store's own size-sold histogram

edge_cases.description: An earring post is specified at a heavier gauge than a standard piercing accepts and will not pass through the lobe
edge_cases.trigger: a post gauge above ~20 ga (thicker than standard piercing)
edge_cases.mitigation: hold posts at the standard ~20-21 ga so they pass a standard lobe piercing

edge_cases.description: An allergy return is treated as a fit problem and 'fixed' by offering a different size instead of a nickel-safe material
edge_cases.trigger: a skin-reaction return coded as size/fit
edge_cases.mitigation: code allergy separately and fix it with a hypoallergenic base metal under the EN1811 limit, not a size change

edge_cases.description: A returned worn plated ring is restocked and resold as new despite surface wear from wearing
edge_cases.trigger: an exchange process that returns used plated pieces to sellable stock
edge_cases.mitigation: inspect and, if worn, write off rather than resell; cost the return as potentially non-resellable

edge_cases.description: The ranking is read as banning rings entirely, dropping a high-demand hero category over size-return fear
edge_cases.trigger: the risk ranking treated as a ban rather than a bias
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the ranking as a bias and launch a hero ring with half sizes, a size guide, and an exchange-first path

edge_cases.description: An international customer orders a ring from a US-only size chart and receives the wrong size due to a system mismatch
edge_cases.trigger: a US-only size chart with no mm-circumference or UK/EU conversion
edge_cases.mitigation: publish inside-circumference-in-mm and a UK/EU/JP conversion so any market can map its size

edge_cases.description: A necklace is sold at a single fixed length with no extender and returned because it sat higher or lower than expected
edge_cases.trigger: a fixed-length chain with no extender or on-model length reference
edge_cases.mitigation: add an extender chain and an on-model length visual to absorb length preference

workflow.action: Partition the inherited categories by fit dimension
workflow.description: Assign each kb1 category to SIZED, LENGTH-CHOICE, or SIZELESS to locate where sizing risk can originate
workflow.gate: every candidate category is assigned to a fit bucket with the sizing-risk-originates-only-in-fit rule stated

workflow.action: Fix the ring sizing systems and conversion
workflow.description: State US/ISO-8653/UK/EU/JP systems and the ~2.55mm-per-size increment with inside circumference as the anchor
workflow.gate: the systems, the increment, and the mm-circumference conversion anchor are stated

workflow.action: Add band-width and comfort-fit fit effects
workflow.description: State that wide/comfort-fit bands wear tighter and the size-up-half rule, with knuckle-governed fit
workflow.gate: the width effect, the size-up-half rule, and knuckle-governed fit are stated

workflow.action: State the necklace/chain and bracelet/bangle standards
workflow.description: State length bands and the extender lever, and split bracelets (adjustable) from rigid bangles (hard-fit)
workflow.gate: the length bands, the extender lever, and the clasp-vs-rigid-bangle split are stated

workflow.action: State the hoop-diameter and earring-gauge standards
workflow.description: State hoop diameter bands and standard 20-21 ga post / 20-18 ga piercing, framing earrings as sizeless
workflow.gate: the diameter bands, the standard post/piercing gauges, and the sizeless framing are stated

workflow.action: Build the fit-tolerance and plating-constraint model
workflow.description: State the half-size fit unit, the smallness of casting/plating variance, and the plating no-resize truth
workflow.gate: the half-size unit, negligible casting/plating variance for fit, and the exchange-not-resize plating truth are stated

workflow.action: Catalogue the adjustable and sizeless low-risk routes
workflow.description: List adjustable constructions and the genuinely sizeless categories as the two routes to low size returns
workflow.gate: the adjustable constructions and the sizeless categories are enumerated with their tradeoffs

workflow.action: Establish the return-driver taxonomy and the sizing link
workflow.description: Enumerate the return reasons and give the reason-code + size-exchange method that measures the sizing share
workflow.gate: the return-reason taxonomy and the reason-code + size-exchange + per-category-rate method are stated with rates flagged [UNKNOWN]

workflow.action: Carry the hygiene and allergy earring return drivers
workflow.description: State the pierced-earring hygiene final-sale norm and the nickel-release allergy driver with EN1811
workflow.gate: the hygiene final-sale norm and the EN1811 nickel-allergy driver are stated as non-size drivers

workflow.action: Set the stocked size range and the pre-purchase fit tools
workflow.description: Give the size-distribution method for the stocked range and the fit tools with their A/B measurement
workflow.gate: the stocked-range method and the fit tools with a before/after size-return measurement are stated

workflow.description: Order sizeless < adjustable < fixed-length < bangle < ring with each mechanism, as a bias not a ban
workflow.gate: the risk ordering with mechanisms and the bias-not-ban framing is stated with rates [UNKNOWN]

workflow.action: Compose the hand-off with the honesty ledger
workflow.description: Deliver per-category rank + size range + fit tools + return-handling, with the [FACT]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] ledger, stopping before the assortment pick
workflow.gate: the per-category spec, the honesty ledger, the clean pre-pick boundary, and the four binding conditions are stated

priority_rationale: The fit-bucket partition, the ring sizing systems, and the necklace/hoop/bracelet standards come first because every fit, tolerance, and return claim depends on knowing a category's fit dimension and its standard; the width effect, fit-tolerance model, and plating constraint next, because they turn the raw standards into how fit is actually governed and why plated pieces cannot be resized; the adjustable and sizeless routes, the return-driver taxonomy, and the sizing-return link then convert fit into the returns causal chain and its measurement method; the hygiene/allergy drivers, the size-distribution and size-guide methods refine the non-size drivers and the pre-purchase levers; and the risk ranking, exchange economics, honesty ledger, and hand-off come last because they compose the answer to 'which categories minimize sizing-driven returns' and pass it, honestly tagged, to the assortment and economics specialists.

dominance_rules.rule: A genuinely sizeless category dominates an adjustable sized one for size-return minimization
dominance_rules.rationale: a category with no fit dimension cannot generate a size return, while an adjustable one still can and adds a feel/durability cost
dominance_rules.trigger: a category can be designed either sizeless or as an adjustable sized piece
dominance_rules.action: choose the sizeless design unless the form inherently requires sizing

dominance_rules.rule: First-time fit accuracy dominates return recovery where resize is impossible
dominance_rules.rationale: plated rings cannot be cheaply resized and earrings are final-sale, so a wrong fit is costly or unrecoverable
dominance_rules.trigger: a fit-risk category is being launched
dominance_rules.action: invest in half sizes, a size guide and to-scale imagery before relying on the return path

dominance_rules.rule: The measured size-coded return rate dominates any a-priori or quoted rate
dominance_rules.rationale: reason-coded, size-exchange-tracked data is the only defensible size-return number
dominance_rules.trigger: a size-return figure is needed for a decision
dominance_rules.action: use the store's measured rate; where absent, state [UNKNOWN] and use only the ranking's direction

dominance_rules.rule: Band width and the size-up rule dominate a bare nominal ring size
dominance_rules.rationale: a single finger size underdetermines fit for wide and comfort-fit bands
dominance_rules.trigger: a wide or comfort-fit ring is listed
dominance_rules.action: publish the band width and the size-up-half rule alongside the nominal size

dominance_rules.rule: Hand-through measurement dominates wrist measurement for rigid bangles
dominance_rules.rationale: a rigid bangle must clear the hand, so a wrist-based size fails
dominance_rules.trigger: a rigid bangle needs a size guide
dominance_rules.action: instruct the widest hand-through measurement or switch to an adjustable/oval bangle

dominance_rules.rule: The correct return reason code dominates the customer's convenience reason
dominance_rules.rationale: misattributing appearance or allergy returns to size mis-credits a size fix and hides the real driver
dominance_rules.trigger: a return reason is ambiguous or strategically stated
dominance_rules.action: verify against the exchange behaviour (same-style-different-size = size) before crediting sizing

dominance_rules.rule: Exchange-first dominates refund for a plated size return
dominance_rules.rationale: an exchange retains the sale where a plated ring cannot be resized and a refund loses it
dominance_rules.trigger: a plated ring is returned for size
dominance_rules.action: offer the correct size as an exchange or store credit before a refund

dominance_rules.rule: The ranking's direction dominates but never bans a high-demand category
dominance_rules.rationale: a high size-return category can still be net-positive with mitigations
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk category has strong demand
dominance_rules.action: launch it with half sizes, a size guide and an exchange path rather than dropping it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Partition categories by fit dimension before assigning any size standard or return risk
anti_rework_rules.prevents: attaching sizing standards or size-return risk to categories that carry no fit dimension and re-doing the analysis

anti_rework_rules.rule: Publish inside-circumference-in-mm plus UK/EU/JP conversions from the first size chart
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a US-only chart that generates international wrong-size returns and a later chart rebuild

anti_rework_rules.rule: List band width and the size-up rule alongside every wide/comfort-fit ring at listing time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: tight-at-knuckle size returns on plated rings that cannot be resized and must be exchanged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stand up reason-code and size-exchange tracking before quoting any size-return rate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fabricated or misattributed size-return number circulating and being retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the stocked size range from supplier defaults plus half sizes, refined by own sales, from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a too-narrow range that manufactures avoidable size returns and a later re-ranging

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide adjustable-vs-sized-vs-sizeless per category before committing SKUs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: launching a fixed-size plated ring where an adjustable or sizeless design would have removed the size-return risk entirely

anti_rework_rules.rule: State the earring hygiene final-sale policy and to-scale imagery at launch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-purchase hygiene disputes and chargebacks that a plain checkout policy would have pre-empted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Route plated size returns to exchange-first, not resize, in the return policy from day one
anti_rework_rules.prevents: promising resizes on plated pieces and damaging finishes, then reworking the return policy

iteration_protocol.trigger: the store accumulates enough reason-coded returns to compute per-category size-return rates
iteration_protocol.action: replace the a-priori direction with measured rates and re-order the risk ranking and hand-off

iteration_protocol.trigger: an A/B or before/after test on a PDP fit tool completes
iteration_protocol.action: update the fit-tool spec and its measured size-return effect

iteration_protocol.trigger: the store's own size-sold histogram becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: supersede the anthropometric/supplier priors and reset the stocked size range

iteration_protocol.trigger: an adjustable plated construction shows a plating-fatigue/quality-return signal
iteration_protocol.action: re-weigh adjustable-vs-sized-vs-sizeless for that category and update the ranking

iteration_protocol.trigger: a base-metal/post material change or a nickel-regulation update lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the allergy-return driver and any affected earring hand-off condition

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cited standard (ISO 8653, EN1811, FTC 16 CFR 23) is revised or a target-market size chart is adopted
iteration_protocol.action: update the affected size/standard nodes and the honesty ledger's [FACT] anchors

iteration_protocol.trigger: the return/exchange policy or a resale-of-returns process changes
iteration_protocol.action: update the exchange economics flow and the return-handling hand-off condition
